situation:
You are the assistant controller for MERIDIAN CRATE AND CARTON, a maker of custom shipping crates and corrugated cartons. The chief financial officer (judge) has asked you to recommend what the company should do about its delivery fleet as it opens its first plant outside the state.

MERIDIAN CRATE AND CARTON is the largest packaging supplier in its region, and its forty delivery trucks have reached the end of their service life. The company's drivers are trained as packaging advisers. They set up pallet systems on the customer's dock, suggest carton and cushioning bundles that ship together at one price, and most of them move into sales jobs after a few years on the route.

Replacing the trucks would take a six-year equipment loan, and those payments would push the out-of-state plant back by about two years. The chief financial officer (judge) has also received a proposal from BLUEROUTE LOGISTICS, a contract carrier that would haul every order for less than the company now spends on its own fleet, freeing the cash the new plant needs right away.

BLUEROUTE LOGISTICS drivers deliver freight and nothing else. Handing them the routes would end the adviser role, the on-dock bundling advice that customers give as their reason for staying, and the training path that has filled most of the sales department. The chief financial officer (judge) wants you to compare the two courses of action against the company's expansion plans and its people, and to recommend one.

You will present your analysis and your recommendation to the chief financial officer (judge) in the chief financial officer's office. The chief financial officer (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas. After your presentation and your answers to the questions that follow, the chief financial officer (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the chief financial officer of MERIDIAN CRATE AND CARTON, the custom crate and carton maker described above. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You want the assistant controller to compare replacing the forty delivery trucks with a six-year equipment loan against handing the routes to BLUEROUTE LOGISTICS, to say what each one does to the expansion, to the adviser role and to the drivers' path into sales, and to recommend one.

After the presentation you will ask these two questions:
judgeQuestions: What would you do in the first month to put your recommendation in place?
Who at the company would you talk to first, and what would you tell them?
